cells.tense: You're in it now — the strength moving between people here is partly yours, and you know it.
cells.ask: Commit one thing you made or know to a direction worth aiming it at — a person to show, a group to teach — sometime today.
cells.core:
The strength here moves because people give it where it's needed, and you're one of the ones giving. What you hand over arrives, and nothing has to be forced about it — the group is steadier for what you've put in, and nobody had to be talked into receiving it. There's a bench where this happens: you put something down, someone picks it up, and the next person gets it from them.

That's exactly the spot where something can grow next. Strength that flows this steadily is free to be aimed, so choose one thing you've been carrying that deserves a direction — not more people helped, just one clear place to point it. Naming where it goes is what turns this steadiness into something that lasts past you.
cells.sheetLine: The support is flowing because you're giving it a place to go.
cells.verb: passing strength along, by measure, to whoever needs it next
cells.place: the common ground where a group's meaning gets handed forward

cells.tense: You're bracing for the point where everybody finally needs what you've got, and you're already supplying it before the ask.
cells.ask: Name one thing you're holding for the group that nobody asked for yet, and set it down until someone actually asks.
cells.core:
There's a picture of this going well: strength shared because people asked and it was there when they did — the group gets what it needs, and you're not used up by handing it over. Nobody has to plan it; it moves as it's wanted, and the giving doesn't pre-empt anyone.

You're running a version of that in advance — already supplying what might be wanted, ahead of anyone saying the word — and that bracing costs the very thing you're supplying for. Give less before it's asked for. Say one thing plainly: "I'm holding this, but nobody's asked." Fairness here isn't keeping score. It's letting the group's own asking do the directing.

cells.tense: The strength to share is standing behind a door you've already closed, and the group can't feel it.
cells.ask: Finish this sentence in a place someone will read it: "What I'd keep alive here is ___," and leave it there for a day.
cells.core:
When this runs as it can, something known gets handed forward — a way of doing things, a story, a practice — and it lands because it was placed with care. People pick it up and carry it without thinking about it; nobody has to decide again each time, and the thing stays warm because it keeps moving.

Right now that habit isn't running. What's kept isn't being passed on, and the group does without what you're holding. Don't push more effort into the starved place. Instead finish one sentence where it can be seen — what you'd keep alive here — and let that finished thing stand on its own.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding what you'd keep alive and not letting it out.

cells.tense: You're already one of the people keeping this group's meaning going, and you talk about it like it keeps going by itself.
cells.ask: Claim one thing you've been doing to keep something here alive, in a sentence someone else can read: "I keep this going because ___" — today.
cells.core:
In plain times, a group's meaning stays alive because people hand it forward — a habit kept, a story retold, a standard held — and it works because someone chose it, this time and last time. You're doing some of that. The support is running.

The credit isn't. You describe the group's continuity as something that just happens, and not as work someone — you — is doing. Claim one piece of it before the day ends: one sentence saying you keep this alive and why. That's the smaller, earlier form of the same strength, and it's the one that builds.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping something alive here, and calling it nobody's doing.

cells.place: the common ground where a group's meaning gets handed forward
